thread.title: Chinese Man bites Apple’s iPhone battery to explode, 4.45 million people witnessed

author: Marcelle Iacocca
title: Chinese Man bites Apple’s iPhone battery to explode, 4.45 million people witnessed
text:
January 24, 2018 Chinese Man bites Apple’s iPhone battery to explode, 4.45 million people witnessed 
In China, a man walked into an electronics store while seeking a new replacement battery for his Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL )’s iPhone. It is not identified yet which store he was in, but on the side of the shop it was written “Professional screen change”. The man started to look closely at the battery to check its authenticity and surprisingly decided to bite down on it, leading the device to explode suddenly in a ball of fire. Despite the fact that the explosion was inches away from the man’s face along with the other spectators, no one have got any injuries according to the report. 
The incidence was captured by the store’s CCTV camera and its video was uploaded on a Chinese video sharing site miaopai.com on Jan 20. Since then about 4.45 million times the video has been watched. 
The teeth of the person possibly caused a disastrous rupture to the casing of the device and suddenly it erupted into a huge ball of fire which engulfed him and the spectators around him. Fortunately, no injuries were reported in the blast, however the sudden explosion startled the individuals present in the store. While responding the video, a Chinese citizen joked the man by saying that the battery is not made of gold so why he bite down it. 
Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL) is decelerating older models of the iPhone with aged batteries after a big uproar over it. The company has started to provide a discount on replacement batteries around the globe, including in China. Last month, the company said that it will offer battery replacements for $29 rather than the usual $79, which has possibly encouraged more people to replace their devices’ batteries. 
However, Chinese electronics stores are scandalously abundant with fake goods so the man tried to check the authenticity of the new battery but obviously his way of testing was wrong. Nonetheless, it’s true that the counterfeit and faulty lithium-ion batteries might explode sometimes or simply get overheat. The man’s way of testing the battery was wrong but it is not clear yet whether the battery exploded due to its fake material or because it was damaged through his teeth. 
In the past, iPhone along with other devices have undergone problems with lithium-ion batteries in addition to overheating. As indicated by the site Digital Trends, there exists three primary reasons that cause a smartphone battery breakdown i.e. overcharging, overheating and applying heavy pressure to the device. Definitely, biting is an act of putting pressure on the battery. About Marcelle Iacocca
